simple.meaning: רָאֶה (râʼeh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “seeing , i.e. experiencing.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Job, beginning at Job 10:15. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רָאֶה (H7202) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: רָאֶה (râʼeh) / H7202 is traced through Job 10:15 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H7202. raeh [ רָאֶה ] adjective seeing , assumed by Thes and others to explain construct עָנְיִי וּרְאֵה Job 10:15 , but improbable; Masoretes apparently intended Imperative (unsuitable); Ew and others וְרֹאֵה ; Di Bu Du (after Lag Gei) עֹ֑נִי רְוֵה drenched (i.e. sated) with affliction.

occurrences.englishText: If I am wicked, woe to me.
